title: Division Facts: Equal Shares, Fact Families and Thinking Multiplication
seo_title: Grade 3 Division Facts Worksheets: Equal Shares and Fact Families (TEKS 3.4H, STAAR)
standard_text: 3.4F recall facts to multiply up to 10 by 10 with automaticity and recall the corresponding division facts; 3.4H determine the number of objects in each group when a set of objects is partitioned into equal shares or a set of objects is shared equally; 3.4J determine a quotient using the relationship between multiplication and division
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 division worksheets for Texas TEKS 3.4F, 3.4H and 3.4J: share equally, make equal groups, number lines, fact families, divide using multiplication facts and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Division splits a total into equal groups.
key_sub: To divide, think of the multiplication fact: 56 ÷ 7 = 8 because 7 × 8 = 56.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Division splits a total into equal groups. 24 ÷ 4 can mean 4 groups (how many in each?) or groups of 4 (how many groups?).
  • Every division fact has a multiplication fact. To find 56 ÷ 7, ask: 7 times what is 56? 7 × 8 = 56, so 56 ÷ 7 = 8.
  • A fact family uses the same three numbers: 4 × 6 = 24, 6 × 4 = 24, 24 ÷ 4 = 6, 24 ÷ 6 = 4.
  • 0 ÷ 5 = 0. 5 ÷ 1 = 5. 5 ÷ 5 = 1.

Examples

Example

Find 42 ÷ 6.

Think: 6 × ? = 42

6 × 7 = 42

Answer: 42 ÷ 6 = 7

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Subtracting: 24 ÷ 4 = 20Division makes equal groups. Use the multiplication fact.
Giving the number of groups when the question asks how many in eachRead the question again: is it asking for each group or the number of groups?
Thinking 0 ÷ 5 = 5If there is nothing to share, each group gets 0.

faq.a: Find the number of objects in each group when a set of objects is shared or partitioned into equal groups.

faq.q: How do I learn division facts?
faq.a: Use multiplication. Every fact like 7 × 8 = 56 gives two division facts: 56 ÷ 7 = 8 and 56 ÷ 8 = 7 (TEKS 3.4F, 3.4J).

faq.q: What are the two meanings of division?
faq.a: Sharing (how many in each group) and grouping (how many groups). Both use the same fact.
You cannot share something into 0 groups. Grade 3 students learn that 0 divided by a number is 0.

items.q: Share 12 counters equally on 6 plates. How many counters go on each plate?
items.e: Deal the counters out one at a time until they are all used. Each plate gets 2, because 6 × 2 = 12.

items.q: 25 counters are put in groups of 5. How many groups are there?
items.e: Count how many groups of 5 you can make from 25: 5 × 5 = 25, so there are 5 groups.

items.q: 12 counters are shared equally on 2 plates. Which division fact matches the picture?
items.e: 12 shared into 2 equal groups gives 6 in each group: 12 ÷ 2 = 6.

These 18 dots are in 3 equal rows. How many dots are in each row?
7 × 9 = 63. Which division fact is also true?
items.e: 7, 9 and 63 make a fact family. 7 × 9 = 63, so 63 ÷ 7 = 9 and 63 ÷ 9 = 7. Division starts with the biggest number, 63.

items.q: 6 × 8 = 48. Which division fact is also true?
items.e: 6, 8 and 48 make a fact family. 6 × 8 = 48, so 48 ÷ 6 = 8 and 48 ÷ 8 = 6. Division starts with the biggest number, 48.

items.q: 4 × 6 = 24. Which division fact is also true?
items.e: 4, 6 and 24 make a fact family. 4 × 6 = 24, so 24 ÷ 4 = 6 and 24 ÷ 6 = 4. Division starts with the biggest number, 24.

items.q: Which fact is in the same fact family as 8 × 9 = 72?
items.e: The fact family for 8, 9 and 72 is 8 × 9 = 72, 9 × 8 = 72, 72 ÷ 8 = 9 and 72 ÷ 9 = 8. 9 ÷ 72 is turned around: division starts with the biggest number.

items.q: Which is not in the same fact family as 4 × 8 = 32?
items.e: The fact family for 4, 8 and 32 is 4 × 8, 8 × 4, 32 ÷ 4 and 32 ÷ 8. 32 ÷ 2 = 16 is true, but it uses 2 and 16, so it is not in this family.

items.q: Which three numbers make a multiplication fact family?
items.e: 4 × 9 = 36, so 4, 9 and 36 make a fact family. 4 + 9 = 13 and 5 + 7 = 12 are adding, and 4 × 8 = 32, not 36.

items.q: Which fact helps you work out 54 ÷ 9?
Which multiplication fact checks 56 ÷ 8 = 7?
items.e: Multiply the answer by the number you divided by: 7 × 8 = 56. Subtracting 8 once does not undo dividing by 8.

items.q: How many 7s make 63?
How many 6s make 36?
items.e: 36 ÷ 6 = ? Skip count by 6s to 36: 6, 12, 18, 24, 30, 36. That is 6 jumps.
